question: How Do I Add a Tracking Number to an Order?
metaDescription: A dedicated shipment-tracking plugin adds a tracking field to the order screen and can automatically email the number and carrier link to the customer.
shortAnswer: Core WooCommerce doesn't include a built-in tracking number field — a dedicated shipment-tracking plugin adds one directly to the order edit screen, letting a tracking number and carrier be recorded per order (or per shipped item, for split shipments), and typically handles emailing that information to the customer automatically, along with a direct tracking link where the carrier supports it.

bodyHtml:
How Tracking Plugins Work

Once installed, a tracking plugin adds a field (or a dedicated meta box) to the order edit screen where staff enter the tracking number and select the carrier from a supported list. From there, the plugin generates the correct tracking URL format for that specific carrier and, depending on configuration, automatically includes it in the order's shipped/completed notification email without any manual email composition.

What to Look For in a Tracking Plugin

  • Support for the specific carriers actually used, since tracking URL formats differ by carrier and a plugin needs to recognize each one to generate a working link.
  • Automatic customer notification, emailing the tracking number and link as soon as it's added, rather than requiring a separate manual step.
  • A customer-facing tracking page or account order view, letting a logged-in customer check tracking status without needing to dig through email.
  • Support for multiple tracking numbers per order, needed if an order ships as multiple separate packages.
  • Bulk tracking upload, useful for stores processing many orders daily, letting tracking numbers be added via a CSV import rather than one at a time.

Setting This Up

  1. Install a shipment-tracking plugin supporting the carriers your store actually uses.
  2. Configure automatic customer email notification once a tracking number is added.
  3. Add tracking numbers as orders ship, using bulk upload if order volume warrants it.
